ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Duke Kahanamoku

code.originalText: Six-month review: repeat echocardiogram after more than 90 days of therapy, the defibrillator decision, iron, the delayed titration step, and plans for the year

text.paragraph: Six-month review: repeat echocardiogram and the defibrillator decision. [S]

Mr. Kahanamoku returns two weeks after his annual wellness visit; at his wish, members of his ʻohana joined him for the defibrillator discussion. He completed all 36 sessions of cardiac rehabilitation in the summer, swam in the pool there for the last month, and now swims three mornings a week in calm water inside the reef with a friend; he has not surfed big waves. He has had no swelling, orthopnea, palpitations, lightheadedness or fainting. The planned increase of sacubitril-valsartan two weeks after his last review did not happen: the nurse called, but he put off the laboratory visit twice because of work, the call was not repeated, and he stayed on the starting dose. He takes every dose of his medicines. Today's echocardiogram shows the ejection fraction has risen from 30% to 38%. [S]

list.item:
Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (I50.22). Much better: NYHA class I to II, KCCQ-12 80, NT-proBNP 620 pg/mL from 2,450, and an ejection fraction of 38% from 30% after more than five months on all four classes. Potassium 4.6 mmol/L and creatinine 1.14 mg/dL (eGFR 70). Sacubitril-valsartan is still at the starting dose because a titration step was missed. [S]
Raise sacubitril-valsartan to 49/51 mg twice daily today; standing blood pressure 104/64 without symptoms allows it.
Metabolic panel in one to two weeks, drawn at the clinic, with nurse calls for further steps.
Continue carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily, empagliflozin, spironolactone 12.5 mg and furosemide 20 mg.

Defibrillator decision (I50.22). The ejection fraction is 38%, above the 35% threshold, after more than 90 days of therapy and years after the infarction, so a primary-prevention ICD is not indicated. QRS 104 ms, so no CRT. He and his ʻohana were told what would change this. [S]
Repeat echocardiogram if symptoms worsen or after further titration if his course changes.
Call 911 for fainting or a racing heartbeat.

Iron deficiency (E61.1). Repleted: ferritin 248 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 27%, hemoglobin 14.1 g/dL. [S]
Iron studies yearly.

The panel due one week after the planned sacubitril-valsartan increase was never drawn, because the increase itself did not happen: he put off the laboratory visit twice for work and the nurse's call was not repeated. No laboratory harm resulted (potassium 4.6, creatinine 1.14 today), but the ARNI stayed at the starting dose for about five months, which may have limited his recovery. Corrective action: laboratory tests drawn at the clinic on the day of each change or by the nurse at home, and nurse calls that continue until each step is done
